method: Founder-reviewed current intelligence registry. Daily discovery remains a separate zero-token watch and does not auto-publish unreviewed findings.

findings.title: Local TT
findings.summary: Direct civic-reporting collision: crowdsourced local infrastructure reporting and tracking; recognized as a 2024 WSA Government & Citizen Engagement winner.
findings.whyFtn: Community Connect must move above commodity complaint reporting into evidence, interoperability, adoption and cross-domain decision support.

findings.title: Pearly
findings.summary: Government-backed citizen engagement app launched June 2026; accepts issue reports with photo/video/location and routes matters to relevant departments.
findings.whyFtn: Benchmark routing, adoption and citizen experience; differentiate through evidence intelligence, regional interoperability and FTN ecosystem integration.

findings.title: CIIF Data Intelligence and Digital Cultural Registry funding
findings.amount: Up to USD100,000 per data-intelligence project; upcoming digital cultural-registry solution programme valued at USD150,000
findings.summary: CIIF funds Caribbean creative-industry data intelligence and lists a 2026 digital solution for national cultural registries/databases; grant calls recur quarterly during the programme cycle.
findings.eligibility: Registered entities in eligible CDB member countries; creative-sector alignment. Minimum 10% contribution may apply to grant beneficiaries.
findings.whyFtn: FTN already owns Screen, creator metadata, Opportunities, Index and intelligence infrastructure that can be configured into a Caribbean cultural-data solution rather than built from zero.

findings.title: Strengthening Statistical Capacity and Interoperable ICT Infrastructure
findings.deadlineConflict: CARICOM Statistics opportunities page states August 31, 2026 while the central CARICOM procurement notice states September 11, 2026. Verify directly before acting.
findings.summary: Current CARICOM procurement directly overlaps FTN's statistics, interoperability and evidence-data architecture.
findings.whyFtn: Even if FTN does not yet meet procurement qualifications alone, this is a high-value partner/consortium signal and validates the regional market for interoperable statistics infrastructure.

findings.title: LAC AI Accelerator
findings.summary: 2026 cohort is closed, but the World Bank says this is expected to become an annual challenge. Requires backing from a public digital authority and accepts public/private/civil-society/academic teams.
findings.whyFtn: Mayor Mode/Mission Control plus Community Connect and ibis-ai can be packaged as a bounded municipal use case; institutional backing is the critical missing asset.

findings.title: AI-Enabled Digital Public Services and Decision Intelligence Platform
findings.organization: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence / World Bank LAC AI Accelerator
findings.summary: Selected 2026 T&T use case integrates predictive analytics and data tools for government decision-making, public-health resilience and climate-disaster preparedness.
findings.whyFtn: FTN's potential edge is citizen evidence + cross-domain provenance + municipal operational workflows; institutional credibility and deployment evidence remain weaker and must be addressed.

findings.title: IDB Caribbean TechLab
findings.summary: IDB emerging-technology laboratory hub for the Caribbean is located in Trinidad and Tobago and focuses on technologies including generative AI, AR/VR, social robots and drones.
findings.whyFtn: A local regional institution can provide validation, technical relationships and visibility without requiring FTN to surrender its platform ownership.

findings.title: SIDS 2.0 Caribbean Digital Future
findings.summary: Regional digital transformation initiative explicitly includes digital public services, transparency, integrated platforms, digital business and civic engagement.
findings.whyFtn: FTN's connected civic and intelligence stack maps directly to multiple stated SIDS 2.0 objectives and offers a Caribbean-owned implementation asset.

findings.title: EU-LAC Digital Accelerator
findings.summary: Running multi-year programme connects corporate challenges with startups/SMEs and provides partnership acceleration; 2026 Call #5 is closed but Caribbean partnerships could receive services valued up to EUR40,000.
findings.whyFtn: Scout should match future challenge owners to already-built FTN capabilities instead of applying generically.

findings.title: President's Award for Innovation in Service Excellence (Pr.A.I.S.E.)
findings.organization: IDB / Trinidad and Tobago public sector
findings.summary: Public-sector innovation award accepts ministries, state entities, municipalities and THA projects in Citizen Experience or Internal User Experience categories.
findings.whyFtn: FTN itself may not be the eligible applicant, but a municipal pilot could become an award pathway and institutional-validation target.
